Incumbent [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] Governor [[Mike Beebe]] ran for re-election, and faced former [[Arkansas Senate|State Senator]] [[Jim Keet]], whom he defeated in a [[Landslide victory|landslide]] to win a second and final term as governor, despite the year being a Republican midterm wave year and Democratic senator [[Blanche Lincoln]] being [[2010 United States Senate election in Arkansas|unseated by a 21-point margin]] on the same ballot. Beebe's re-election was also despite Republicans on the same ballot gaining the offices of lieutenant governor, secretary of state, and commissioner of state lands. Beebe's vote percentage and margin of victory was the highest of any Democratic gubernatorial candidate in the country in 2010. This was also the only Arkansas gubernatorial election since Democrat [[David Pryor]] in 1976 in which either major party nominee won every county. As of 2026, this, alongside the concurrent treasurer, state auditor, and attorney general elections, is the last time Democrats won any statewide election in Arkansas. Because of this, this was the last time a Democrat was elected the governor of Arkansas to date. This was also the last time in which a gubernatorial nominee and a lieutenant gubernatorial nominee of different political parties were elected in Arkansas, and the last time that Arkansas simultaneously voted for gubernatorial and U.S. Senate candidates of different political parties. ==Candidates== ===Democratic Party=== *[[Mike Beebe]], incumbent governor ===Republican Party=== *[[Jim Keet]], former [[Arkansas Senate|state senator]] ===Green Party=== *[[Jim Lendall]], former [[Arkansas House of Representatives|state representative]] and [[Arkansas gubernatorial election, 2006|2006]] gubernatorial nominee ==General election== ===Predictions=== {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center" |- !
